summary:
We developed an interactive space mission design game that allows to manage a complete space mission. In this escape-room-style simulator, players face real-world aerospace scenarios where they must balance competing demands.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming the abstract concepts of space mission planning into a hands-on experience. Players must make critical engineering decisions and manage limited resources using previous mathematical, chemistry and physics knowledge—like spacecraft mass, energy, fuel, and possible crisis that a space mission may encounter—while navigating emergencies. Every decision directly impacts their mission's success, teaching them how each choice shapes the outcome.

This project is important because it makes learning about space exploration dynamic and accessible. Instead of just reading theory, students develop critical problem-solving skills, practice teamwork, and experience the actual complexities of NASA missions, ultimately fostering a deeper interest in science and technology.
details:
Here are the details of our project, broken down by the key areas of your submission:

  • How it works Our project, "Astraea-1", is an interactive web-based escape room simulator. Players progress through four chronological mission phases (Earth Prep, Transit, Surface EVA, and Reentry). They must monitor a live Heads-Up Display (HUD) tracking spacecraft integrity, oxygen, power, and crew vitals. Players interact with 2D room schematics to solve math and physics-based puzzles—like calculating water-to-food payload ratios or calibrating drill torque—while dealing with real-time consequences and emergencies if they make mistakes or defer maintenance.
    • Code & Interface: We built the final prototypes as self-contained HTML5 web applications utilizing CSS3 and JavaScript, with custom inline SVG code for the visual room maps.
    • Audio: We used the native Web Audio API to code a procedural, non-saturated ambient synthesizer soundtrack from scratch, without relying on external MP3s.
    • AI Engine: We used Google Gemini as the dynamic "Game Master" and Mission Control console, utilizing strict system prompt engineering and Markdown data architecture to manage the game's state machine.
    • Research Tools: We used Boolean search queries on the NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS) and ESA archives to gather authentic flight protocols.
  • Creativity Our project is innovative because it merges rigorous real-world space data with escape room mechanics and artificial intelligence. Instead of reading textbooks, players get a dynamic, personalized narrative powered by Gemini. We also found creative ways to visualize dense data, turning walls of text into intuitive, color-coded 2D maps (e.g., blue for inspection, red for emergencies).
  • Factors Considered We had to carefully balance realistic aerospace constraints—like mass, fuel budgets, signal lag, and ECLSS life support limits—with playable game mechanics. We also heavily considered data limitations and AI behavior; we built strict cause-and-effect matrices and prompt boundaries to prevent the AI from hallucinating, ensuring the simulation remained scientifically grounded while still being fun.
